A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiSSL study. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices A–C support reliable comparison. The added appendix subsection and pagination changes do not create material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream classification experiments in Table 1, a pre-training-duration study in Figure 2, and latent-feature analyses in Section 4.4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original downstream classification results, pre-training-duration experiments, and latent-feature analyses, including revised numerical results and plots.

M1.justification: The bilevel objectives, implicit-gradient approximation, alternating updates, backbone adaptation, and training pipeline remain unchanged. Equations 2–7 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same method; the hyperparameter revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions pre-train on STL10U and evaluate the same 14 downstream datasets. The Flowers pre-training-duration experiment and the nine datasets represented in the latent-feature plots are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 2 retain the conventional SSL pipeline, labeled Only FT, as the comparator. Feature plots retain the conventional pretext backbone comparison. The newly discussed meta-learning methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.2 specifies a BiSSL warm-up peak learning rate of 1.0, whereas v1 described matching the baseline's 4.8 except for duration. Table 3 changes Food's learning rate and FashionMNIST's weight decay, and Table 4 revises downstream fine-tuning hyperparameters throughout. These are reported setting revisions within the retained splits, models, metrics, training budgets, and search procedure.

E4.justification: The existing pre-training-duration sensitivity analysis receives revised curves in Figure 2, and the representation-alignment analysis receives updated BiSSL feature plots in Figures 3–11. These replace evidence for the same analytical questions; no new component ablation or robustness scenario is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten evaluations with different random seeds, report means and standard deviations, and bold significant comparisons in Table 1. Figure 2 retains uncertainty bands. Changed deviations and significance markings are result updates, with no change to the stated statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises BiSSL results while retaining Only FT values. For example, STL10L top-1 changes from 90.6% to 90.2%; CUB200 top-1 changes from 45.6% to 47.1%, while top-5 changes from 75.2% to 72.1%. Figure 2 and the feature plots also change. These are result revisions under revised settings, not same-setting performance gains; the broad finding of improved or comparable performance remains.

T1.justification: v1's Appendix A derivation becomes Appendix A.1 without changing its fixed projection-head, convexity, or invertible-Hessian assumptions, or Equations 8–9. New Appendix A.2 provides conceptual comparisons with meta-learning, without adding formal definitions, proofs, or mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: connecting pre-training and fine-tuning through bilevel optimization, providing a practical training pipeline, achieving improved or comparable downstream performance, and improving feature alignment. The central novelty and empirical scope claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that BiSSL requires full access to pre-training data and pretext tasks, and proposes investigating subsets and alternative tasks. It also expands discussion of more efficient BLO solvers. The existing uncertainty about larger models and tasks remains.

D1.justification: v1 promises public code and pre-trained weights; v2 states that they are publicly available, retaining the same printed repository link. Section 4.2.2 and Appendix B revise documented hyperparameters. The conjugate-gradient implementation, batching instructions, and other reproduction details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 distinguishes BiSSL from MAML, Sign-MAML, and iMAML through objective structure, task-specific optimization, and parameter reinitialization. Additional citations cover visual SSL, language models, and BLO solvers, including DINOv2 and LLaMA. The existing Section 2 discussion and overall positioning are retained.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in the introduction, future-work discussion, and acknowledgments. Appendix A gains a broader title and separates the existing derivation into A.1 alongside new A.2, with corresponding cross-reference updates. The main narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 has revised curves and rescaled vertical axes, and the BiSSL panels in Figures 3–11 are redrawn. Appendix material reflows around the added text. All four tables and eleven figures remain, with their principal display formats preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency and positioning by explicitly identifying the pre-training data/task access requirement in Section 5.1, explaining its relationship to meta-learning in Appendix A.2, and reporting code and weights as available. The mixed score revisions under changed settings do not establish a performance improvement. The gains are principally clearer applicability and documentation, while the method, formal justification, and evaluation breadth remain stable.
